title: The Element That Hid for 134 Years: Lanthanoid Contraction
subject: Chemistry
objective: Hafnium sat in zircon beside zirconium but was found only in 1923, 134 years after zirconium, because the two are almost the same size (Zr 160 pm, Hf 159 pm) despite Hf's 32 extra electrons and extra shell. Between them in period 6 sit the 14 lanthanoids, across which the size of atoms and Ln³⁺ ions decreases steadily (La³⁺ ≈ 103 pm → Lu³⁺ ≈ 86 pm): the lanthanoid contraction. Each step adds a proton while the new electron enters 4f, which shields poorly (s > p > d > f), so the outer electrons are pulled in. The contraction cancels the expected increase in period 6: Zr ≈ Hf, Nb ≈ Ta, Mo ≈ W; Zr and Hf (and the lanthanoids) are hard to separate; and the basicity of Ln(OH)₃ decreases from La to Lu.

tf.q: 4f electrons shield the outer electrons very effectively.
Zr and Hf have almost the same atomic radius.
The basicity of Ln(OH)₃ increases from La to Lu.
Nb and Ta have nearly equal radii.
The lanthanoid contraction makes Zr and Hf easy to separate.
tf.explain: It makes them very hard to separate.

ar.a: Hf has nearly the same radius as Zr.
ar.r: The lanthanoid contraction cancels the size increase expected from the extra shell.

ar.a: Basicity of Ln(OH)₃ decreases from La to Lu.
ar.r: The smaller Ln³⁺ holds OH⁻ more strongly, so the Ln–OH bond is more covalent.

short.q: Define lanthanoid contraction and give its cause.
short.solution: The steady decrease in size of atoms and Ln³⁺ ions from La to Lu; each step adds +1 nuclear charge while the new 4f electron shields poorly, so the outer electrons are pulled in.

short.q: Give three consequences of the lanthanoid contraction.
short.solution: 4d and 5d elements of a group have nearly equal radii (Zr/Hf, Nb/Ta, Mo/W); Zr and Hf (and the lanthanoids) are hard to separate; basicity of Ln(OH)₃ decreases from La to Lu.

short.q: Why must zirconium for nuclear reactors be purified from hafnium?
short.solution: Zr hardly absorbs neutrons, but Hf absorbs thermal neutrons hundreds of times more strongly; Hf occurs with Zr because of their equal size, so it must be removed.
